sections.title: Intro
points: 1.0 lands 11 December - so before it does, I'm ranking every PoE 2 league so far.
Two years of Early Access: the launch, four challenge leagues and one event league.
Hook: tease the most controversial placement up front - don't reveal it yet.
deeper: For scale: 578k players on Steam at the Early Access launch - and 1.0 goes free-to-play.

sections.title: How I'm ranking them
points: The league mechanic itself - fun to engage with
Loot and economy - did it feel rewarding? Issues?
The patch around it - balance, endgame, how the game felt that season.
Player retention - did people keep playing, did it get better or fall off?
Worth mentioning: every one of these league mechanics is now core, but youre ranking them based on how they were on release.

sections.title: 0.1 - Early Access launch
sections.subtitle: 6 December 2024 - no challenge league
points: No challenge league - everyone just played Early Access Standard.
Three acts plus Cruel, six classes, about 50 areas.
Huge launch: over a million copies sold, a 578k Steam peak.
So busy GGG's support team drowned in tickets.
+ Common praise: act bosses really good, some called it the best ARPG launch ever,  and the feel of combat's amazing.
-  Common complaints: ruthless loot, slow movement, and a bare endgame.
prompts: Was 0.1 the most fun you had despite being the least finished?
What did 0.1 get right that later patches lost?
Do you think the Reddit praise for the campaign was justified, or was it rose-tinted?
deeper: Reddit threads compared 0.1 endgame to a placeholder - only maps and no pinnacle bosses.
Some argued the slow pace was intentional and good; others said it killed replayability.

sections.title: 0.2 - Dawn of the Hunt
sections.subtitle: 4 April - 26 August 2025
points: The first real league - though nothing was exclusive, it all went straight into core.
The mechanic: Azmerian Wisps - you chase them, and every monster they touch gets juiced.
Plus Rogue Exiles that drop their own uniques, and unique Strongboxes.
The big draw: the Huntress and spears.
+ Common praise: the Huntress hype pulled almost 240k players back on day one.
- Common complaints: nerfs everywhere, a slow punishing campaign, relentless monsters, gutted endgame loot.
It got review-bombed to 'Mostly Negative' - GGG admitted it felt too slow and hotfixed within a week.
deeper: Ran about 20 weeks.
Also new: Smith of Kitava, Tactician and Lich ascendancies; 100+ uniques, 100+ supports, 8 maps.
Spears felt unsatisfying to many - parry and spear throw got buffed in that first hotfix.
Expedition, Simulacrum and early Corrupted Nexus were called badly overtuned.

sections.title: 0.3 - Rise of the Abyssal
sections.subtitle: The Third Edict - 29 August - 9 December 2025
points: PoE 2's first proper full league.
The mechanic: Abyss fissures - kill the pack, Abyssals climb out, close it for a trove. Sometimes it opens the Abyssal Depths.
The crafting hook: bones and desecrated mods - reveal at the Well of Souls and pick one of three.
And the patch around it was massive: Act 4, interludes instead of Cruel, a support gem overhaul.
+ Common praise: Act 4, the interludes and Cruel being gone - reception was overwhelmingly positive.
- Common complaints: freezes in big Abyss pulls, sudden deaths to stacked elite mods, worthless uniques, a dry endgame.
prompts: Was desecration the best crafting addition PoE 2 has had?
Shortest league of the lot - did it end too early or at the right time?
deeper: Shortest league: ~14.5 weeks.
Abyss went core in 0.4 and got its own Atlas passive tree.
Abyssal Lich alternate ascendancy came with the Abyss mechanic.
0.3.0b spread Abyss pits out to stop huge packs freezing the game, and made Abyssals bindable as Spectres.
Forum feedback: campaign loot felt much more bountiful - but Act 4 bosses felt rushed to some.

sections.title: 0.4 - Fate of the Vaal
sections.subtitle: The Last of the Druids - 12 December 2025 - 25 May 2026
points: The mechanic: Vaal structures - sacrifice monsters to power your way into Atziri's Temple.
You build the temple yourself - rooms level up the rooms next to them, Atziri waits at the top.
Came with the Druid - shapeshifting, Talismans, the Wyvern.
+ Common praise: the Druid, and GGG doubling temple rewards within a week.
- Common complaints: temples were slow for little reward, confusing to path, and you lost rooms after the Architect.
The January hotfix killed the 'snake' temples making hundreds of Divines - late builders felt robbed.
Tavern Talk's take: a rough start, then the temple endgame won back the people who stayed.
Abyss went core in 0.4 and got its own Atlas passive tree
prompts: Agree with - slow start, great endgame?
Longest league of the lot - earned it or overstayed?
deeper: Longest league: ~23.4 weeks.
250+ new passives and the first Lineage Supports (8+).
Big CPU optimisations shipped with 0.4.
Moved to core in 0.5.
GGG's own words a week in: temple rewards 'simply don't scale enough to make temples worth doing'.
NeverSink: Vaal Cultivation Orb prices 'plummeted' from abuse - part of the hotfix was reverted on 5 Jan.
Forum takes ranged from 'a much worse Sanctum' to '0.3 was a much better experience'.
Vaal crafting: corruption benches, Architect's Orb, Vaal Cultivation Orb, transcendent limbs.

sections.title: 0.5 - Runes of Aldur
sections.subtitle: Return of the Ancients - 29 May 2026 - early December 2026
points: The mechanic: a Remnant in every area - pick the item you want with runeshapes, then survive the waves for it.
More runes means more waves and nastier mods - but better items.
Verisium and Runeforging - and Runic Ward
And it shipped with the full endgame overhaul - GGG called it their biggest update ever.
+ Common praise: the endgame rework, the Arbiter fights, Remnants being fun - 'damn near a home run'.
- Common complaints: crashes and stutter, a brutal death penalty in juiced maps, Runic Ward bricking items.
prompts: Deterministic crafting - did it make loot feel worse or better?
Runic ward - was it a big addition to the game or just another mechanic that you half ignore?
deeper: 23 Kalguuran skills, 13 Alloys, Fluxes, Ancient and Mythical runes all come out of Remnants.
Moved to core in 0.5.5; still running until just before 1.0.
Players said they played this league more than any since launch.
Replaying the campaign on new characters still called tedious; Delirium's goals felt unclear.
Runeforging also upgrades low-level uniques so they stay usable late.

sections.title: Bonus: 0.5.5 - Forbidden Rites (event league)
sections.subtitle: 4 September 2026 - runs alongside Runes of Aldur
points: An event league: Ritual in every campaign area, with levelling rewards.
Boss rituals chain - beat a boss and it joins the next ritual's waves; tribute buys uniques.
+ Common praise: it makes levelling genuinely fun and generous.
- Common complaints: sold as a one-month event, then quietly extended to 1.0 - plus a run of bugs.
deeper: Sacred Blooms bring back the Viridian Wildwood and wisps on your Atlas.
Trial of Chaos finally lets you leave mid-run.

sections.title: The full board - and what 1.0 needs to learn
points: Reveal the full board - call out the biggest gap between tiers.
1.0's league is Conquerors of Wraeclast - armies, castles, sieges, three factions on one shared Atlas.
You said on Exilecon, your reaction was: 'straight up my alley' - RTS into PoE - why?
Your 1.0 start: Infernalist? Demon Magus?
1.0 also adds Acts 5-6, the Shadow and Duelist, ~110 effectively new uniques, a 70-node Atlas tree.
prompts: Which past mechanic should 1.0 learn the most from?
deeper: Biggest swing on the board: 0.2's review bomb vs 0.5 being called 'damn near a home run'.
Recurring theme across every league: performance and crashes in the first weeks.

sections.title: Outro
points: Ask: where would you put each league? Drop your tier list in the comments.
Plug the 1.0 launch subathon.

Demon Magus.summary: The Demon Magus is a new Infernalist ascendancy meta gem that summons a reviving demon minion which casts spells you socket into it, with spell costs paid by you and scaling damage based on socketed skill variety.
changes: New Infernalist ascendancy skill: Demon Magus meta gem summons a Reviving Demon Magus that casts socketed Spells
Cost of Spells cast by the minion are paid by you
Spells cast by the minion cost 50% less
Minion deals 15% more Damage per different socketed Skill
Quality grants Minions 0-20% more Maximum Life
You can socket multiple spells as well as supports of your choosing into it
